overview: 18 papers: 5 HIGH PRIORITY, 9 RELATED / POSSIBLY INTERESTING, and 4 LOW PRIORITY. The central themes are zero-entropy invariant measures and dense multiplicative orbits, topological dynamics of weighted shifts, the circle as a topological fractal, hyperplane absolute winning, and Hausdorff dimensions of Diophantine intersections. Related papers cover measurable delay semiflows, local linearization, escaping-set topology, stability undecidability, approximation statistics, minimal groupoids, periodic magnetic geodesics, and Mather measures.

paper.title: Delay equations with measure-valued coefficients: From Carath\'eodory solutions to measurable semiflows
paper.abstract: We study linear delay differential equations whose delay terms are represented by time-dependent finite signed measures. This framework accommodates discrete, distributed, and singular delay contributions without requiring continuity of the coefficient paths in time. We establish well-posedness in the Carath\'eodory sense and sequential dependence of solutions on the measure-valued parameters under almost-everywhere weak-* convergence and a common total variation bound. A central part of the analysis associates a signed measure on the time--delay domain with each coefficient path and establishes an equivalent integral formulation. This representation yields three equivalent characterizations of a $\sigma$-algebra on the parameter space suited to measurability of the continuation operator. A measurable fixed-point argument then provides measurability of the solution maps, despite the possible failure of continuity in the product weak-* topology. For coefficients generated by a measure-preserving base flow, these results lead to measurable linear skew-product semiflows on continuous and absolutely continuous phase spaces. Under additional ergodic hypotheses and the assumption of a finite top Lyapunov exponent, eventual compactness and regularization yield Oseledets decompositions with the same Lyapunov exponents and multiplicities on both spaces.

analysis.relevance_note: Measurable skew-product semiflows and Oseledets decompositions provide a direct connection to ergodic and invariant-measure dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For coefficients generated by a measure-preserving base flow, these linear delay equations generate measurable linear skew-product semiflows despite limited time regularity. Under additional ergodic assumptions and a finite top Lyapunov exponent, the authors obtain matching Oseledets data on two phase spaces.
analysis.problem: Establish well-posedness, parameter dependence, and measurable evolution for linear delay equations allowing discrete, distributed, and singular delays without continuity of coefficient paths in time.
analysis.main_result: The authors prove Carathéodory well-posedness and sequential parameter dependence under almost-everywhere weak-* convergence with a common total variation bound. For coefficients generated by a measure-preserving base flow they construct measurable linear skew-product semiflows on continuous and absolutely continuous phase spaces. Eventual compactness and regularization yield Oseledets decompositions with identical Lyapunov exponents and multiplicities on both spaces, under additional ergodic hypotheses and a finite top Lyapunov exponent. The precise additional ergodic hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Associate a signed measure on the time-delay domain to each coefficient path and use an equivalent integral formulation.
Characterize a parameter sigma-algebra in three equivalent ways and apply a measurable fixed-point argument.
Use eventual compactness and regularization for the comparison of Oseledets decompositions.
analysis.context: The abstract connects delay equations with measurable dynamical systems even when solution-map continuity in the product weak-* topology may fail.

paper.title: Complete characterization of planar $C^1$ linearizability and optimal conjugacy regularity
paper.abstract: We establish a complete characterization of local $C^1$ linearizability for planar diffeomorphisms. For every prescribed hyperbolic real Jordan form, we obtain necessary and sufficient integrability conditions on the modulus of continuity of the derivative for local $C^1$ linearizability. These criteria reduce to three canonical thresholds: the classical, polynomially weighted, and squared-logarithmically weighted Dini conditions. Each threshold is optimal: whenever the corresponding condition fails, we construct a diffeomorphism with the identical linear part that is not locally $C^1$ linearizable. For every non-hyperbolic linear part, explicit polynomial counterexamples show that smoothness alone cannot guarantee even local topological linearization. Beyond $C^1$ existence, we determine the optimal regularity for the derivative of the linearizing conjugacy in every hyperbolic case, with the optimality established by counterexamples.

analysis.relevance_note: Local conjugacy, hyperbolicity, and the obstruction to topological linearization connect this smooth-dynamics paper to the profile.
analysis.tldr: For planar diffeomorphisms with a prescribed hyperbolic real Jordan form, the authors give sharp derivative-modulus integrability criteria for local \(C^1\) linearization. They also obtain optimal conjugacy-derivative regularity and polynomial counterexamples for nonhyperbolic linear parts.
analysis.problem: Determine sharp conditions for local \(C^1\) linearization of planar diffeomorphisms and the regularity of the derivative of a linearizing conjugacy.
analysis.main_result: For every prescribed hyperbolic real Jordan form, the criteria reduce to classical, polynomially weighted, or squared-logarithmically weighted Dini conditions. Failure of the corresponding condition permits a diffeomorphism with that same linear part that is not locally \(C^1\) linearizable. The authors also state optimal regularity of the conjugacy derivative in every hyperbolic case. For every nonhyperbolic linear part, explicit polynomial counterexamples show that smoothness alone does not guarantee even local topological linearization. The precise integrability formulas and regularity moduli: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Construct counterexamples to establish optimality of the thresholds and conjugacy regularity.
Use explicit polynomial counterexamples for nonhyperbolic linear parts. The proof method for the sufficient linearization criteria: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract distinguishes regularity-based linearization criteria in hyperbolic cases from obstructions that persist for smooth nonhyperbolic maps.

paper.title: Normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
paper.abstract: We study real-analytic, planar, maps, at a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We construct normal forms for them, when they admit a real-analytic first integral. We prove that a second first integral, when it exists, forces their linearisation. We consider both the resonant and the non-resonant case, whether the maps preserve a symplectic form or not. The second first integral is allowed to be smooth, real-meromorphic or real-analytic.

analysis.relevance_note: Normal forms and linearization near elliptic fixed points are conceptually related to smooth conjugacy dynamics; the abstract states no entropy or dimension result.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct normal forms for real-analytic planar maps near elliptic fixed points when a real-analytic first integral exists. They state a linearization result involving a second first integral, whose precise additional requirements are not specified in the abstract.
analysis.problem: Describe local normal forms and the effect of first integrals on linearization near an elliptic fixed point of a real-analytic planar map.
analysis.main_result: Normal forms are constructed under the existence of a real-analytic first integral. The authors state that a second first integral forces linearization, allowing that second integral to be smooth, real-meromorphic, or real-analytic. Both resonant and nonresonant cases are considered, with or without preservation of a symplectic form. The precise condition distinguishing the second integral from the first: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Construction of normal forms. Further proof details: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The stated setting is local elliptic dynamics and integrability; the abstract treats resonance and symplectic preservation as separate possibilities.

paper.title: Dense times-b orbits from times-a invariant sets and measures, in zero entropy
paper.abstract: Let $a,b$ be multiplicatively independent integers. We prove that if $\mu$ is a zero-entropy non-atomic $\times a$-invariant measure on $[0,1]$, then $\mu$-a.e.~$x$ has dense $\times b$-orbit. Related statements follow for many closed $\times a$-invariant sets, and in particular we conclude the existence of irrational numbers with minimal complexity in base $a$ and maximal complexity in base $b$. We extend~these results to commuting endomorphisms of the torus under an irreducibility and hyperbolicity condition.

analysis.relevance_note: Zero entropy, invariant measures, dense orbits, and contrasting digit complexity directly match the strongest interests.
analysis.tldr: For multiplicatively independent integers \(a,b\), a zero-entropy non-atomic \(\times a\)-invariant measure on \([0,1]\) gives full measure to points with dense \(\times b\)-orbits. The authors also obtain invariant-set and digit-complexity consequences and extensions to commuting torus endomorphisms under additional conditions.
analysis.problem: Understand how zero-entropy invariance under multiplication by \(a\) constrains orbit density under multiplication by a multiplicatively independent integer \(b\).
analysis.main_result: If \(a,b\) are multiplicatively independent integers and \(\mu\) is a zero-entropy non-atomic \(\times a\)-invariant measure on \([0,1]\), then \(\mu\)-almost every point has dense \(\times b\)-orbit. Related statements hold for many closed \(\times a\)-invariant sets, yielding irrational numbers with minimal complexity in base \(a\) and maximal complexity in base \(b\). Extensions to commuting torus endomorphisms require irreducibility and hyperbolicity. The exact conditions for those extensions and definitions of the stated complexity extremes: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract links zero-entropy invariant measures to orbit density under a different multiplicative action and to contrasting base-expansion complexity.

paper.title: Dynamics of Weighted Backward Shifts on Ces\`aro Spaces of Rooted Trees
paper.abstract: We study the dynamics of weighted backward shifts on Ces`aro spaces associated with leafless locally finite rooted trees. We first characterize their boundedness in terms of adjacent level cardinalities and edge weights. We then characterize their $\mathcal{F}$-transitivity by a growth condition involving level cardinalities, products of weights along paths, and a level-dependent Ces`aro factor. As consequences, we obtain criteria for hypercyclicity, weak mixing, topological ergodicity, and topological mixing. We also characterize the existence of nonzero orbit limit points and chaotic weighted shifts, the latter in terms of normalized fixed points and unit flows satisfying an explicit summability condition. Examples show that $\mathcal{F}_{\underline{d}>0}$-transitivity need not imply frequent hypercyclicity, that a nonhypercyclic weighted shift may nevertheless have a nonzero orbit limit point, and that topological mixing need not imply chaos.

analysis.relevance_note: Transitivity, mixing, hypercyclicity, and chaos of shifts are central topological-dynamics themes.
analysis.tldr: Weighted backward shifts on Cesàro spaces of leafless locally finite rooted trees admit criteria for boundedness and several topological dynamical properties. Examples separate positive-lower-density transitivity, frequent hypercyclicity, mixing, chaos, and the existence of nonzero orbit limit points.
analysis.problem: Characterize topological dynamical properties of weighted backward shifts in terms of the underlying rooted tree and its weights.
analysis.main_result: The authors characterize boundedness using adjacent level cardinalities and edge weights, and \(\mathcal{F}\)-transitivity using a growth condition involving level cardinalities, path weight products, and a level-dependent Cesàro factor. They obtain criteria for hypercyclicity, weak mixing, topological ergodicity, and topological mixing, as well as characterizations of nonzero orbit limit points and chaos. Chaos is expressed using normalized fixed points and unit flows satisfying a summability condition. Examples show that \(\mathcal{F}_{\underline{d}>0}\)-transitivity need not imply frequent hypercyclicity, a nonhypercyclic shift can have a nonzero orbit limit point, and topological mixing need not imply chaos. Exact growth and summability formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Counterexamples distinguish the stated dynamical properties. Further proof methods for the characterizations: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract provides tree- and weight-dependent criteria and separates dynamical properties that need not coincide in this operator setting.

paper.title: Compartmental Epidemiological Models: Discussing Fundamental Elements via the SIR Model
paper.abstract: We present a didactic treatment of compartmental disease spread modeling centered on the SIR framework, aimed at mathematics education. Our focus is on how modeling choices encode transmission mechanisms and data-collection practices. We begin by stating the structural hypotheses of compartmental models, including population partitioning, homogeneous mixing, flow closure, and Markovian transitions. We then derive the basic SIR dynamic equations in both continuous-time (differential equations) and discrete-time (difference equations) settings. A key goal is to clarify the distinction between density-dependent and frequency-dependent transmission. We do this by constructing the force of infection from the contact rate, prevalence, and per-contact transmissibility while tracking units and interpretations. We go beyond the usual mass-balance SIR model by introducing the discrete Kermack-McKendrick perspective through the cumulative force of infection. This naturally leads to discrete SIR updates with an exponential escape probability term. We also derive Bernoulli-based exponential formulations for both density- and frequency-dependent transmission, interpret these probabilistically over observation intervals, and obtain the associated discrete infectivity kernel. This highlights how geometric infectious survival emerges from per-step removal. The paper includes reproducible, introductory-level Python code to implement the basic discrete SIR model, the continuous SIR model, and the exponential discrete variants. We provide instructors with an example of parameter estimation from prevalence data using least squares, along with guidance on interpretation and limitations. This framework is designed to help teachers integrate model assumptions, units, simulation, and inference in a coherent introduction to infectious disease modeling.

analysis.relevance_note: A didactic treatment of epidemiological modeling and parameter estimation, without a central entropy, dimension, symbolic, or topological-dynamics theme in the abstract.

paper.title: A counterexample to Eremenko's conjecture
paper.abstract: The escaping set of a transcendental entire function consists of those points that tend to infinity under iteration. Eremenko asked whether every connected component of this set is unbounded. In arXiv:2108.10256, we constructed transcendental entire functions for which the escaping set has prescribed compact connected components; in particular, it may have a singleton component. This disproves the conjecture. In this note, we give an introduction to the problem, aimed at a general mathematical audience. We also sketch a variant of the construction in which a prescribed half-strip is an oscillating wandering domain and an escaping point lies on its boundary. The account is based on the second author's lecture at the 2026 International Congress of Basic Science.

analysis.relevance_note: The topology of escaping sets and wandering domains connects the note to complex dynamics; no entropy or dimension theorem is stated.
analysis.tldr: This expository note explains the authors' earlier counterexample to Eremenko's conjecture about connected components of escaping sets. It also sketches a variant with a prescribed half-strip as an oscillating wandering domain and an escaping point on its boundary.
analysis.problem: Explain whether connected components of the escaping set of a transcendental entire function must be unbounded.
analysis.main_result: The authors describe their earlier construction in arXiv:2108.10256 of transcendental entire functions whose escaping sets have prescribed compact connected components, including a singleton, disproving Eremenko's conjecture. The present note introduces the problem for a general mathematical audience and sketches a variant with a prescribed half-strip as an oscillating wandering domain and an escaping boundary point.
methods: Exposition of the earlier counterexample and a sketch of a variant construction. Detailed construction steps: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The note is based on the second author's 2026 International Congress of Basic Science lecture and presents an earlier disproof rather than claiming it originates in this note.

paper.title: Lyapunov stability of polynomial vector fields is undecidable
paper.abstract: We show that there are integers $N$ and odd $D$ such that no algorithm can decide, from the rational coefficients of a homogeneous polynomial vector field F of degree $D$ in dimension $N$, whether the origin is Lyapunov stable for $\dot Y=F(Y)$. This proves, for some large and unoptimized dimension and degree, a conjecture of V. I. Arnold.

analysis.relevance_note: Undecidability of qualitative stability is conceptually adjacent to dynamical complexity, but the abstract states no entropy, coding, or dimension connection; the relevance is therefore uncertain.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove that deciding Lyapunov stability of the origin is impossible algorithmically for rational homogeneous polynomial vector fields in some fixed dimension and odd degree. The dimension and degree are large and unoptimized.
analysis.problem: Determine whether an algorithm can decide Lyapunov stability of the origin from the rational coefficients of a homogeneous polynomial vector field.
analysis.main_result: There exist integers \(N\) and odd \(D\) such that no algorithm decides, from the rational coefficients of a homogeneous polynomial vector field \(F\) of degree \(D\) in dimension \(N\), whether the origin is Lyapunov stable for \(\dot Y=F(Y)\). The abstract states that this proves a conjecture of Arnold for some large, unoptimized dimension and degree. Numerical values of \(N,D\) and the undecidability reduction: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The stated conclusion concerns algorithmic decision of stability for a fixed but unoptimized choice of dimension and odd degree.

paper.title: Dissipative Evolutions in Metric Spaces
paper.abstract: We study a novel class of evolution variational inequalities (EVI) driven by bifunctions $\mathsf{b}:\mathrm{D} \times \mathrm{D} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined on a subset $\mathrm{D}$ of a metric space $(\mathrm{X},\mathrm{d})$ and satisfying a natural dissipativity condition $$\mathsf{b}(x,y)+\mathsf{b}(y,x)\le \eta \mathrm{d}^2(x,y).$$ We provide general conditions for existence, stability, regularity, approximation and asymptotic behavior of solutions, by proposing a metric framework that generalizes the classical structure of evolutions driven by monotone operators in Hilbert spaces. A motivating application is the setting of minimax and multispecies coupled gradient flows, in which each of $N$ species evolves in the direction of steepest descent of its own energy functional and the joint system is not a gradient flow of any single energy. To construct solutions, we introduce a variational movement scheme (VMS), a time discretization scheme in which each update is a saddle point of a metrically penalized bifunction, generalizing the classical minimizing movement/ JKO scheme for single species gradient descent. In the coupled multispecies case, the VMS reduces to a Nash equilibrium problem. We prove existence of discrete solutions to the VMS via a general approach which combines dissipativity of $\mathsf{b}$ with a new notion of convexity along suitable $\textit{barycentric interpolations}$ (which is inspired by convexity along generalized geodesics, a crucial notion for gradient flows). Together, these conditions provide a zeroth-order notion of game-theoretic monotonicity applicable to general metric spaces without linear structure.

analysis.relevance_note: Metric evolution variational inequalities and coupled gradient flows are the focus; the abstract gives no central connection to entropy, pressure, dimension, symbolic dynamics, or topological dynamical invariants.

paper.title: Extreme value laws for intrinsic Diophantine approximation on spheres
paper.abstract: We study intrinsic Diophantine approximation on the sphere $S^d$, measured by the quality of the best rational approximation available at a given height. We show that, for $d\geq 3$ and along sufficiently sparse sequences of heights, these quantities have a Weibull limit distribution and the associated counting functions are asymptotically Poissonian.

analysis.relevance_note: Statistical laws in intrinsic Diophantine approximation are potentially related to the profile, but the abstract does not specify a fractal-dimension or group-action connection; relevance remains uncertain.
analysis.tldr: For intrinsic rational approximation on \(S^d\) with \(d\geq 3\), the authors obtain a Weibull limit for best-approximation quality along sufficiently sparse height sequences. Associated counting functions are asymptotically Poissonian.
analysis.problem: Determine limit distributions for the quality of the best rational approximation available at a given height on a sphere.
analysis.main_result: On \(S^d\), for \(d\geq 3\) and sufficiently sparse sequences of heights, the stated approximation-quality quantities have a Weibull limit distribution and associated counting functions have asymptotically Poisson laws. Precise sparsity assumptions, normalization, and distribution parameters: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract concerns intrinsic approximation on spheres and extreme-value/counting statistics, with an explicit dimensional restriction and a sparsity requirement.

paper.title: A characterization of simplicity of reduced groupoid C*-algebras
paper.abstract: We show that, for a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff \'etale minimal groupoid with compact unit space, simplicity of the reduced groupoid C*-algebra implies the existence of a comeager set of unit points with C*-simple isotropy group. Combining this result with work of Christensen and Neshveyev on exotic completions of isotropy group algebras, we show that the converse implication is also true. Finally, we construct a Hausdorff \'etale minimal groupoid with an isotropy group whose induced exotic completion differs from its reduced group C*-algebra, answering a question of Christensen and Neshveyev.

analysis.relevance_note: Minimal topological groupoids, isotropy, and a comeager condition provide a connection to the group-action and topological side of dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff étale minimal groupoid with compact unit space, simplicity of its reduced \(C^*\)-algebra is equivalent to having a comeager set of units with \(C^*\)-simple isotropy groups. The authors also construct an example separating an induced exotic isotropy completion from the reduced group algebra.
analysis.problem: Characterize simplicity of reduced groupoid \(C^*\)-algebras in terms of isotropy and investigate whether induced exotic isotropy completions can differ from reduced group \(C^*\)-algebras.
analysis.main_result: Under second countability, local compactness, the Hausdorff and étale conditions, minimality, and compactness of the unit space, simplicity of the reduced groupoid \(C^*\)-algebra implies a comeager set of unit points with \(C^*\)-simple isotropy groups. Combining this with work of Christensen and Neshveyev gives the converse under the stated setting. A further construction produces a Hausdorff étale minimal groupoid with an isotropy group's induced exotic completion different from its reduced group \(C^*\)-algebra.
methods: Combine the simplicity implication with Christensen and Neshveyev's work on exotic completions of isotropy group algebras.
Construct a groupoid exhibiting the difference between induced exotic and reduced isotropy completions. Construction details: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The example answers a question of Christensen and Neshveyev, while the equivalence relates algebraic simplicity to a topological largeness condition on isotropy.

paper.title: The circle as a topological fractal
paper.abstract: We prove that no family of two continuous self-maps witnesses that the circle is a topological fractal, answering a question of Karasov\'a and the present author. Since three maps are known to suffice, this bound is optimal. In contrast, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are two continuous self-maps of the circle, depending on $\varepsilon$, whose images cover the circle and an integer $N$ such that every composition of $N$ of them has image of diameter less than $\varepsilon$. Thus two maps suffice at any prescribed scale, but no fixed pair works at all scales.

analysis.relevance_note: Topological fractals and the distinction between contraction at one scale and at all scales directly match topological dynamics and fractal geometry.
analysis.tldr: Exactly three continuous self-maps are needed to witness the circle as a topological fractal. Two maps can meet the stated covering and contraction condition at any prescribed scale, provided the pair may depend on that scale.
analysis.problem: Determine whether two continuous self-maps can witness the circle as a topological fractal and compare this with contraction at a single prescribed scale.
analysis.main_result: The authors prove that no pair of continuous self-maps witnesses the circle as a topological fractal; since three maps are already known to suffice, that bound is optimal. For every \(\varepsilon>0\), however, there is a pair of continuous self-maps, allowed to depend on \(\varepsilon\), whose images cover the circle, and an integer \(N\) such that every composition of \(N\) of these maps has image diameter less than \(\varepsilon\). The pair and composition length are chosen after the scale; the result does not provide a fixed pair working at all scales.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The negative result answers a question of Karasová and the author. The positive result isolates the quantifier distinction between a scale-dependent pair and one pair valid at every scale.

paper.title: Periodic Magnetic Geodesics with Every Low Energy: Existence and Localization
paper.abstract: Let $(Q,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold equipped with a non-identically zero magnetic field represented by a closed $2$-form $\beta$. We allow $Q$ to be non-compact and do not assume that the metric $g$ is complete. We prove that if the magnetic strength, defined as the pointwise norm of $\beta$, attains a strict local maximum on a non-empty compact set $K$, then every sufficiently low energy level carries a contractible periodic magnetic geodesic of the pair $(g,\beta)$ localized near $K$. More precisely, such orbits exist in every neighborhood of $K$, and their lengths converge to zero with the energy. In particular, if $Q$ is compact, then every sufficiently small energy level carries a contractible periodic magnetic geodesic. We also show that, in general, neither the non-emptiness nor the compactness of $K$ can be omitted. Our proof relies on the calculus of variations of the Lagrangian action functional, and uses several new ideas. More precisely, we overcome: (i) the non-exactness of $\beta$ by restricting the minimax to the set of short loops; (ii) the non-completeness of $g$ by combining a compactification of $Q$ with Thom's Jet Transversality and a blow-up for sequences of magnetic geodesics with energy tending to zero; (iii) the possible non-compactness of Palais--Smale sequences by the positivity of the Ricci magnetic curvature for low energy established by the first-named author. Unlike previous work, Struwe's monotonicity argument cannot be used for our purposes, and we rely on a two-Lyapunov-function argument due to Abbondandolo and Majer.

analysis.relevance_note: Existence and localization of periodic orbits connect the paper to geometric flow dynamics, although no entropy, dimension, coding, or rigidity result is stated.
analysis.tldr: Under a strict local maximum condition for magnetic strength on a nonempty compact set, every sufficiently low energy level has a contractible periodic magnetic geodesic localized nearby. The manifold need not be compact and its metric need not be complete.
analysis.problem: Find and localize contractible periodic magnetic geodesics at every sufficiently low energy on a Riemannian manifold \((Q,g)\) with a non-identically zero closed \(2\)-form \(\beta\).
analysis.main_result: If the pointwise norm of \(\beta\) attains a strict local maximum on a nonempty compact set \(K\), then every sufficiently low energy level carries a contractible periodic magnetic geodesic of \((g,\beta)\) near \(K\). Such orbits can be found in every neighborhood of \(K\), with lengths tending to zero as the energy tends to zero. If \(Q\) is compact, every sufficiently small energy level has a contractible periodic magnetic geodesic. In the general localization statement, neither nonemptiness nor compactness of \(K\) can be omitted.
methods: Use the calculus of variations for the Lagrangian action and restrict the minimax to short loops to address nonexactness of the magnetic form.
Combine compactification, Thom's Jet Transversality, and a blow-up for magnetic geodesics with energy tending to zero to handle metric incompleteness.
Use positivity of low-energy Ricci magnetic curvature against noncompact Palais-Smale sequences and the two-Lyapunov-function argument of Abbondandolo and Majer.
analysis.context: The abstract explicitly allows noncompact manifolds and incomplete metrics, and says that Struwe's monotonicity argument is unavailable for this purpose.

paper.title: $\mathbf{Bad}(\mathbf{r};\mathbf{s})$ is Hyperplane Absolute Winning
paper.abstract: Given an $m$-dimensional weight $\mathbf{r}$ and an $n$-dimensional weight $\mathbf{s}$, we prove that the set of $(\mathbf{r};\mathbf{s})$-badly approximable $m\times n$ matrices is hyperplane absolute winning on $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$. This fully answers a question \cite[Question 8.2 (iii)]{Kl} of D. Kleinbock in 1998.

analysis.relevance_note: The central hyperplane absolute winning property of a Diophantine set is closely aligned with the profile's fractal-geometry interests; the abstract does not itself state a dimension formula.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove that \((\mathbf{r};\mathbf{s})\)-badly approximable \(m\times n\) matrices form a hyperplane absolute winning set in \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). They state that this fully answers a question of Kleinbock from 1998.
analysis.problem: Determine the hyperplane absolute winning property of the set of badly approximable matrices associated with an \(m\)-dimensional weight \(\mathbf{r}\) and an \(n\)-dimensional weight \(\mathbf{s}\).
analysis.main_result: For the weights \(\mathbf{r}\) and \(\mathbf{s}\) in the abstract, the set \(\mathbf{Bad}(\mathbf{r};\mathbf{s})\) of weighted badly approximable \(m\times n\) matrices is hyperplane absolute winning on \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). The precise admissibility conditions defining a weight: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The authors identify their theorem as a complete answer to Kleinbock's 1998 question. Further historical comparisons: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Position: A Dynamical Systems Perspective is Needed to Advance Time Series Modeling
paper.abstract: Time series (TS) modeling has come a long way from early statistical, mainly linear, approaches to the current trend in TS foundation models. With a lot of hype and industrial demand in this field, it is not always clear how much progress there really is. To advance TS forecasting and analysis to the next level, here we argue that the field needs a dynamical systems (DS) perspective. TS of observations from natural or engineered systems almost always originate from some underlying DS, and arguably access to its governing equations would yield theoretically optimal forecasts. This is the promise of DS reconstruction (DSR), a class of ML/AI approaches that aim to infer surrogate models of the underlying DS from data. But models based on DS principles offer other profound advantages: Beyond short-term forecasts, they enable to predict the long-term statistics of an observed system, which in many practical scenarios may be the more relevant quantities. DS theory furthermore provides domain-independent theoretical insight into mechanisms underlying TS generation, and thereby will inform us, e.g., about upper bounds on performance of any TS model, generalization into unseen regimes as in tipping points, or potential control strategies. After reviewing some of the central concepts, methods, measures, and models in DS theory and DSR, we will discuss how insights from this field can advance TS modeling in crucial ways, enabling better forecasting with much lower computational and memory footprints. We conclude with a number of specific suggestions for translating insights from DSR into TS modeling.

analysis.relevance_note: A position paper on machine-learning-based time-series modeling and dynamical systems reconstruction, without a central entropy, dimension, symbolic, or topological-dynamics result in the abstract.

paper.title: Set-Based Value Function Characterization and Neural Approximation of Stabilization Domains for Input-Constrained Discrete-Time Systems
paper.abstract: Analyzing nonlinear systems with stabilizable controlled invariant sets (CISs) requires accurate estimation of their domains of stabilization (DOS) together with associated stabilizing controllers. Despite extensive research, estimating DOSs for general nonlinear systems remains challenging due to fundamental theoretical and computational limitations. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for estimating DOSs for controlled input-constrained discrete-time systems. The DOS is characterized via newly introduced value functions defined on metric spaces of compact sets. We establish the fundamental properties of these value functions and derive the associated Bellman-type (Zubov-type) functional equations. Building on this characterization, we develop a physics-informed neural network (NN) framework that learns the value functions by embedding the derived functional equations directly into the training process. The proposed methodology is demonstrated through two numerical examples, illustrating its ability to accurately estimate DOSs and synthesize stabilizing controllers from the learned value functions.

analysis.relevance_note: Control-oriented stabilization domains and neural value-function approximation are central; no strong connection to the priority topics is stated.

paper.title: On the inhomogeneous discounted Hamilton-Jacobi equations
paper.abstract: In this paper, we study the family of inhomogeneous discounted Hamilton-Jacobi equations \begin{equation}\label{hjs1} \lambda(x)u+h(x,d_x u)=c \quad \tag{$\ast$} \end{equation} on a closed manifold $M$ with a non-identically vanishing discount factor $\lambda(x)$. There is a critical value $c_0\in[-\infty,\infty)$ such that \eqref{hjs1} admits a viscosity solution if $c>c_0$ and no solution if $c<c_0$. Inspired by the recent development \cite{RWY} on the stability theory of viscosity solutions, for $\max_M \lambda>0$ , we show that the equation admits an asymptotically stable solution if and only if $c>c_0$. In this case, we determine the basin of the stable solution and investigate the long time behavior of the solution semigroup associated to \eqref{hjs1}. In particular, we relate the lowest convergence rate to the integral of $\lambda$ over Mather measures, which leads to an asymptotic behavior of Mather measures when $c$ goes to infinity. Assuming $c\geqslant c_0$ and the equation admits a solution, we classify ergodic Mather measures and locate their distribution in the phase space.

analysis.relevance_note: Ergodic Mather measures, their phase-space distribution, and convergence of a solution semigroup provide an explicit invariant-measure connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors study solvability and stability of inhomogeneously discounted Hamilton-Jacobi equations, with a critical parameter separating existence and nonexistence. They relate convergence rates to integrals over Mather measures and classify ergodic Mather measures under stated solvability assumptions.
analysis.problem: Study viscosity solutions, asymptotic stability, and associated Mather measures for \(\lambda(x)u+h(x,d_x u)=c\) on a closed manifold \(M\), with a non-identically vanishing discount factor \(\lambda\).
analysis.main_result: There is a critical value \(c_0\in[-\infty,\infty)\) such that viscosity solutions exist for \(c>c_0\) and do not exist for \(c<c_0\). Under \(\max_M\lambda>0\), an asymptotically stable solution exists if and only if \(c>c_0\). In that case the authors determine its basin and study the long-time solution semigroup; they relate the lowest convergence rate to the integral of \(\lambda\) over Mather measures and obtain asymptotic behavior of these measures as \(c\) tends to infinity. Assuming \(c\geq c_0\) and existence of a solution, they classify ergodic Mather measures and locate their phase-space distribution. The abstract does not assert unconditional existence at \(c=c_0\). Further assumptions on \(h\) and exact classification and convergence formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: The abstract connects viscosity-solution stability with Mather measures and distinguishes strict supercritical solvability from the additional existence assumption used at or above the critical value.

paper.title: Well and badly approximable sets, and rapid winning
paper.abstract: The set of $\tau$-approximable numbers, $\mathcal W(\tau)$, has genuinely fractional Hausdorff dimension, whereas the set of inhomogeneously badly approximable numbers, $\Bad^\gamma$, has full Hausdorff dimension. We determine the Hausdorff dimension of their intersection by introducing the $\Psi$-rapid game, a scale-sensitive refinement of the rapid game of Hatefi and Simmons (preprint 2024). For every approximation function $\psi$, we prove that $\mathcal W(\psi)\cap\Bad^\gamma$ is strong $\Psi$-rapid winning for a natural gauge $\Psi$ determined by $\psi$. Unlike Schmidt-type games, whose winning property always implies full Hausdorff dimension, the $\Psi$-rapid game is calibrated to a prescribed Diophantine scale, so that the resulting dimension bound depends explicitly on the decay of $\Psi$. In particular, for $\psi(q)=q^{-\tau}, \tau\ge1,$ we recover the exact Jarn\'ik--Besicovitch dimension, that is, $$ \HD\bigl(\mathcal W(\tau)\cap\Bad^\gamma\bigr)=\frac{2}{\tau+1}.$$

analysis.relevance_note: Hausdorff dimension of Diophantine intersections and a winning game adapted to approximation scales directly match fractal-dimension interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors introduce a scale-sensitive rapid game to study intersections of well-approximable and inhomogeneously badly approximable sets. For power-law approximation with exponent at least one, they obtain the exact Hausdorff dimension of the intersection.
analysis.problem: Determine the Hausdorff dimension of intersections between well-approximable and inhomogeneously badly approximable numbers using a winning notion that retains dependence on the approximation scale.
analysis.main_result: For every approximation function \(\psi\), the authors prove that its well-approximable set intersected with the inhomogeneously badly approximable set is strong \(\Psi\)-rapid winning for a natural gauge \(\Psi\) determined by \(\psi\). The resulting dimension bound depends explicitly on the decay of \(\Psi\). For \(\psi(q)=q^{-\tau}\) with \(\tau\geq 1\), the Hausdorff dimension of the intersection equals \(2/(\tau+1)\). The precise gauge and general dimension bound: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Introduce the \(\Psi\)-rapid game as a scale-sensitive refinement of the rapid game of Hatefi and Simmons.
analysis.context: The abstract contrasts its scale-dependent dimension bounds with the full-dimension consequence of Schmidt-type winning games and identifies the power-law dimension as the Jarník-Besicovitch value.
